messages:
alex: heads up — right after the 23:46 prod push we're seeing p95/p99 blow up and a surge of 504/5xx gateway errors. dashboards: https://internal.grafana/r/xyz. paging @maya for oncall.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created (INC-2450006789) — elevated gateway timeouts detected; paging oncall.
maya: oncall here, thanks for the ping. alex — is rollback an option or do you want to try a quick mitigation? any deploy id?
alex: deploy id = a12cd3b. commit diff included this runtime change to batching/kv behavior. logs show repeated upstream read timeouts and long kernel waits:```
[2025-11-03T23:47:12Z] ERROR handler: upstream read timeout, client=10.2.3.4 path=/v1/generate status=504
[2025-11-03T23:47:12Z] WARN runtime: kernel_wait_ms=3200 queue_depth=120
```
deploy-bot: deploy a12cd3b -> prod finished at 2025-11-03T23:46:10Z. Rollback command: `/deploy rollback a12cd3b`
maya: ok i'll initiate rollback now. notifying SRE to watch infra while rollback runs.
maya: `/deploy rollback a12cd3b` -> started. ETA ~2m.
deploy-bot: rollback a12cd3b -> started by @maya.
chris: quick question — do we know if this affects Dedicated customers or only hosted? alex?
alex: initial impact: both hosted API and some Dedicated pools in us-west. Error-rate spike ~5% of overall requests, but concentrated on long sequences and some K/V cache-heavy routes. top-affected customer buckets: 3 enterprise tenants (ids masked).
sanjay: paging CS and account success now. emma can you open a bridge for CS & SE?
emma: on it — creating slack bridge and sending templated outbound to top 3 accounts. copying support ticket IDs to the incident.
chris: any immediate mitigations besides rollback? can we throttle long sequences or force KV-cache bypass?
alex: we tried a quick runtime flag toggle against a canary host: flipping `runtime.kvcache.enabled=false` decreased mean kernel_wait and cut p99 by ~40% on canary but not feasible cluster-wide without deploy/rolling change.
maya: rollback completed — deploy-bot reports success. `/deploy rollback a12cd3b` -> succeeded at 23:50:05Z.
deploy-bot: rollback a12cd3b -> succeeded.
ops-bot: observed metrics post-rollback: p95 back to baseline, p99 reduced to expected levels. See graphs: https://internal.grafana/r/xyz?view=post-rollback
alex: confirmed — p99 back down, 504s declined to normal. sample logs now show normal tail latencies:```
[2025-11-03T23:51:12Z] INFO handler: request served in 12ms status=200
```
maya: assigning follow-up: eng-runtime to run a targeted postmortem, include canary results, kvcache eviction trace, and batching change. severity downgraded, but we should track root cause.
sanjay: CS notified customers and created high-priority support cases for the 3 tenants.
emma: posted customer-facing note in bridge and queued personalized outreach.
chris: hypothesize: change in continuous-batching interaction with KV cache eviction under high seq-length load — produced head-of-line stalls on some GPU hosts. will reproduce in runtime test infra.
maya: good. next steps: (1) eng-runtime owns postmortem ticket ENG-3001, (2) add an automatic smoke-check after deployment that runs a short high-seq workload against a canary, (3) improve alerting to catch kernel_wait increases before 5xx climb.
alex: adding logs & flame graphs to ENG-3001. I'll attach the canary toggle results and the offending commit.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2450006789 status: mitigated -> monitoring. severity: S2 (reduced). Pager rotation: cleared.
maya: closing oncall handoff — if metrics hold for 30m I'll mark incident resolved. thanks everyone for quick responses :thumbsup:
pager-bot: resolved alert: gateway-timeout-spike.
chris: noted for postmortem — will own the runtime reproducer.
alex: closing thread from my side when postmortem ticket is created. great job team. :rocket:
